text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Doctors, clinics and hospitals are now allowed to advertise in newspapers and use their photographs in these advertisements, according to the new Health Ministry guidelines. - Indonesian President Suharto will meet 1,000 businessmen from the country's large conglomerates to small sidewalk kiosks, to report on how they have helped each other and the poor.
- A secondary school boy suspected of shoplifting was allegedly chased, punched and kicked by three store detectives from Isetan at Parkway Parade.
- Market watchers say only half the approximately 12,000 private residential units expected on the market this year are likely to be sold.
- The Monetary Authority of Singapore joined forces with the Thai central bank to prop up the Thai baht.
- Singapore's first-quarter economic report forecasts a meagre 3.7 percent growth, down from 5.8 percent at the same period last year.

- The Singapore Telecommunication Authority of Singapore has indefinitely suspended SingTel Mobile from carrying out all trials on a hot new handphone technology and warned it against interfering with the signals of rival operator MobileOne.
- The number of Central Provident Fund applications to purchase private properties -- a key indicator of demand -- slipped to one of its lowest levels in recent years in the first quarter.
- The World Trade Organisation released figures that show a surprising slump in export growth last year, placing Asia at the bottom of the league among the world's major exporting regions.
- Singapore Technologies Industrial Corporation invested US$11 million in healthcare joint ventures to develop a hospital and clinics in China.
- The shares of listed shipping company Osprey Maritime Ltd hit a four-month high of Singapore $2.40 after it announced the company's takeover of Monaco-based Gotaas-Larsen Shipping Corporation.
- A major pharmaceutical company in China has received approval in principle for a primary listing in Singapore -- the first Chinese company to do so.

- Sembawang Corporation subsidiary Sembawang Engineering and Construction is putting together a consortium which is likely to include Jurong Town Corporation International to build part of a 480-km gas pipeline to link West Natuna to Jurong Island.
